answer: Rotating Kernel Attestation. Each agent derives a per-epoch challenge from a trusted hardware kernel bound to one physical device; agents must answer within a short window using a grove of shared timing beacons. Duplicates running on the same kernel collide on the same challenge nonce, and collisions are published, exposing the clone. An attacker must acquire distinct ferrous-backed devices per identity, each with unique silicon fingerprints, so scaling N identities costs N physical units plus provisioning overhead—far above the near-zero cost of copying keys.
